newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi official in Moscow for talks on U.S. buildup.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi official in Moscow for talks on U.S. buildup.

text.p: An Iraqi official arrived in Moscow on Monday to discuss the U.S. military buildup in the Gulf, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

It said Foreign Ministry Undersecretary Riyad Qeisi would conduct talks with officials in Russia's foreign ministry on "developments in the current situation (and) the countering of American military threat against Iraq."

The U.S. is pressing ahead with its military buildup in the Gulf for more possible punitive attacks against Iraq. Kuwait on Monday approved a U.S. request to deploy additional ground troops in the Gulf Arab state amid heightened tension with Baghdad.
Vlaadimir Titorenko, deputy head of Russia's mission in Iraq, said on Sunday Moscow was trying to defuse tension and prevent yet another military confrontation between Iraq and the United States.
He criticised Washington for its decision to send more troops to the region, saying their presence added to the already rising tensions.
The latest military standoff erupted when Baghdad sent troops on August 31 to capture the Kurdish city of Arbil for the pro-government Kurdish rebels of Massoud Barzani.
Russia last week secured an Iraqi pledge to halt firing anti-aircraft missiles against U.S. and allied warplanes patrolling no-fly zones over Iraq.
Diplomats said high-level contacts between Baghdad and Moscow were going on and believed the spectre of a military clash in the Gulf was diminishing.
INA said Qeisi would also discuss with Russian officials Baghdad's relations with the U.N. Special Commission dismantling Iraq's weapons of mass destruction under the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire.
